findings.title: limitFunction drops every caller argument before invoking the wrapped function
findings.cause: The returned wrapper is declared as a zero-argument arrow and schedules `function_()` with no forwarded rest arguments.
findings.impact: Any limited function that depends on parameters receives `undefined` values at runtime, even though the TypeScript declaration exposes a generic argument-preserving wrapper.
findings.evidence: index.js:121-124 returns `() => limit(() => function_())`; index.d.ts:133-136 declares `limitFunction<Arguments extends unknown[], ReturnType>(function_: (...arguments_: Arguments) => PromiseLike<ReturnType>, options: Options): (...arguments_: Arguments) => Promise<ReturnType>`. Focused probe `limitFunction(async value => value, {concurrency: 1})('kept')` printed `undefined`.
findings.reproduction_or_test: node --input-type=module -e "import {limitFunction} from './index.js'; const limited = limitFunction(async value => value, {concurrency: 1}); console.log(await limited('kept'));"

findings.title: limit.map omits the mapper index for non-array iterables
findings.cause: `limit.map` computes whether the input is an array and passes `undefined` as the mapper index for every other iterable.
findings.impact: Set, iterator, and generator inputs violate the documented `Array.from(iterable, (item, index) => limit(mapperFunction, item, index))` behavior, so index-dependent mappers break for supported iterable inputs.
findings.evidence: index.js:107-113 uses `iterableIsArray ? index : undefined`; readme.md:78-84 and index.d.ts:30-43 state that the mapper receives item value and index for an iterable. Focused probe over `new Set(['a','b'])` printed `[["a",null],["b",null]]`, where JSON null is the stringified `undefined` index.
findings.reproduction_or_test: node --input-type=module -e "import pLimit from './index.js'; const limit = pLimit(1); console.log(JSON.stringify(await limit.map(new Set(['a','b']), (value, index) => [value, index])));"

findings.title: pLimit({concurrency}) enables rejectOnClear by default despite the documented false default
findings.cause: The options-object destructuring sets `rejectOnClear = true`, while the top-level variable and public documentation say the default is false.
findings.impact: The numeric and options-object forms are not equivalent: `pLimit({concurrency: 1}).clearQueue()` rejects pending promises with `AbortError` even when the caller did not opt in, which can unexpectedly fail `Promise.all` users.
findings.evidence: index.js:4 initializes `rejectOnClear` to false, but index.js:6-8 changes the default to true for an options object. readme.md:46-52, readme.md:149-155, and index.d.ts:99-106 document `Default: false`. A focused probe with `pLimit({concurrency: 1})` printed `AbortError`; the same clear path with `pLimit(1)` remained `still-pending`.
findings.reproduction_or_test: node --input-type=module -e "import pLimit from './index.js'; const limit = pLimit({concurrency: 1}); const running = limit(() => new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 30))); const pending = limit(() => 'never'); await Promise.resolve(); limit.clearQueue(); try { await pending; console.log('resolved'); } catch (error) { console.log(error.name); } await running;"

findings.title: Falsey non-boolean rejectOnClear values bypass runtime validation
findings.cause: The validation condition checks `rejectOnClear && typeof rejectOnClear !== 'boolean'`, so falsey non-booleans are accepted instead of rejected.
findings.impact: Invalid JavaScript callers can silently pass `0`, `null`, or an empty string for a documented boolean option, hiding configuration mistakes and producing different behavior from truthy invalid values.
findings.evidence: index.js:12-14 only throws for truthy non-booleans; index.d.ts:99-106 and readme.md:46-52 define the option as boolean. Focused probe printed `0:accepted`, `null:accepted`, and `:accepted`.
findings.reproduction_or_test: node --input-type=module -e "import pLimit from './index.js'; for (const value of [0, null, '']) { try { pLimit({concurrency: 1, rejectOnClear: value}); console.log(String(value)+':accepted'); } catch (error) { console.log(String(value)+':'+error.name); } }"
